headline: ABB Robotics has added an AI Robot Trainer tool to its camera-guided robot system, which it says can cut the time to set up a robot vision job by up to 90 percent and robot cycle times by up to half.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a product launch from a major robot maker, but the performance figures are the company's own best-case claims.
importance_line: Factories and system builders could set up camera-guided robots with less AI expertise, but the 90 and 50 percent figures are ABB's own "up to" claims with no independent test reported.
summary: Assembly Magazine reports that ABB Robotics says its new AI Robot Trainer lets factories and system integrators train, deploy and keep improving camera-guided robot applications without special expertise in building AI models, for jobs such as picking parts, bin picking, inspection, sorting and assembly. ABB says commissioning, the time to get a robot system working, falls by up to 90 percent and cycle times by up to 50 percent, but these are company figures for the best case.
notes: Product announcement read as a company release; no customer result or test is given, so machine_action is false.
